answer: Every answer stakes a claim on a public mesa: the ledger keeps one live signature per path through the trellis of previously graded work, and that path is derived from the author's own history. Two heads under one controller plan alike, so the second claim lands on ground the first already holds. It pays nothing, and it voids the claim beneath it, since the original can no longer seed a future answer. A lone agent risks one answer; a farm of a hundred loses all hundred, each added head collapsing the plume of paths it rose through.
